title: Shaken subjective faith can still be true — unlike defective ‘scientia’
source_text: XXXIV. Quod si quis dicat istud tantum probare certitudinem fidei, quam vocavimus ante subjectivam, esse scientiarum certitudine minorem, non vero certitudinem fidei objectivam, de qua jam est quaestio: Respondeo fidem illam quae actu in fidelibus tentationibus variis quatitur, & luctatur cum diffidentia, non definere esse veram fidem. Si quis vero minus perceptam haberet vim demonstrationis alicujus Geometricae, & de veritate conclusionis dubitaret, in eo non esset veri nominis scientia. Atque hoc ipso patet scientiam per se & ex suo genere dubitationem magis excludere quam fidem.
pass_a_gloss: But if anyone say that this only proves that the certainty of faith which we formerly called subjective is less than the certainty of the sciences, not the objective certainty of faith concerning which the question now is: I answer that that faith which is actually shaken in the faithful by various temptations and wrestles with distrust does not cease to be true faith. But if anyone had less perceived the force of some Geometric demonstration and doubted of the truth of the conclusion, in him there would not be science of the true name. And by this itself it is plain that science of itself and from its own kind excludes doubt more than faith does.
pass_b_english: Objection: only subjective faith-grade is below scientia.
Reply: tempted/wrestling faith can still be true faith.
Weak grasp of a geometric proof ≠ true scientia — scientia excludes doubt more by kind.
